docs.heading_path: Demand Planning in Maestro – Setting the scene
docs.snippet:
The objective of the Maestro Demand Planning application is to create an unconstrained consensus demand forecast that combines multiple functional forecast perspectives, weighted and adjusted as part of a highly collaborative process, and all orchestrated and documented within a single planning system.
In this section, some of the foundational information for the IXOM Demand Planning solution in Maestro will be described.

docs.heading_path: Consensus Demand Planning: Create Consensus Demand Plan (Unconstrained Demand Plan)
docs.snippet: The next step in the Demand Planning process amalgamates final inputs from Demand Planners and Product Managers to create the Consensus Demand Plan (Unconstrained Demand Plan). Maestro can be configured to automatically disaggregate the consensus demand for the first 3 Months into daily/weekly buckets, if required.

It will be possible for the Demand Planner to work across multiple scenarios depending on where in the IXOM process flow, he/she is. An illustration of the scenario Structure for Demand Planning can be seen below. (Scenario structure to be added later)

This is a modified PDR.

The Demand Review is a meeting held once a month - typically in week 2 of every month. The purpose of this meeting is to align on the aggregated unconstrained Demand Plan, prioritise the decisions required, ensure decision statements are completed in preparation for the Demand Review and where the aggregate business plan lands compared to the budget, gain clear visibility of volume assumptions/risks & opportunities, and agree on recommendations for the Supply Review. The horizon of the plans considered in this process is 18-24 months.

IXOM follows their own way of calculating the safety stock based on the defined service level, Mean Normal Deviation cap limits applied, lead time and the forecast. The Product Manager maintains the Service Level Target, MND Cap limits, and then based on the formula provided in Safety Stock Management, the Safety Stock will be calculated.
After Safety Stock is calculated, there is a concept of cycle stock which accumulates the demand within the delivery calendar and creates a single order to cover the whole demand i.e. cycle stock. At the end, the Product Manager reviews the Safety Stock and o

The Dispatcher works out a distribution plan by considering the consolidated demand coming from different medium and the logistics available such as Truck availability, driver’s availability, etc. The CAP plant Dispatcher Plans are brought into Maestro as Demand Orders and the system plans against that.
At each Part/Site (Delivery Location), Consensus Demand Plan (Forecast) gets consumed by the demand orders, if there is any unconsumed forecast exists, then system considers that in the Total Demand. After that if there are any safety stock requirements present, system makes sure the safety sto

Based on the system-suggested planned orders, the supply plan is evaluated to determine how effectively it meets the demand orders received from the Dispatcher.  Orders should be firmed when approaching the lead time or firming period, and existing firm orders can be updated in response to any changes in demand orders. Also, if there is any ad-hoc (non-regular) inventory transfer possible to fulfill the shortage at any location, inventory transfer can be created manually.
L3 Process – Constrain and Create Distribution Plan (Short-term)

The system takes the monthly forecast and the safety stock requirements, generates the long-term supply plan, from that you will understand the inventory projections throughout the planning horizon and do the rough-cut capacity planning.
